title: cli_hours_active_7d overcounts: CountCLIActivityHours counts rows, not distinct hours
description:
VERIFIED BUG, independent of the repo_id issue and arguably worse.

apps/api-go/internal/db/queries/auth.sql:17-22:
  -- name: CountCLIActivityHours :one
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS hours FROM cli_activity WHERE user_id = $1 AND hour_bucket >= $2;

It counts ROWS. The dedup key is (user_id, COALESCE(repo_id,''), hour_bucket), so one user in one hour produces 1 NULL row + 1 row per repo whose detail was fetched.

CONCRETE: a single 'ox status' in an initialized project fires GET /cli/repos/{repo_id} (status.go:422) AND GET /cli/repos (status.go:426) back to back -> 2 rows in one hour bucket -> reported as 2 hours active.

BLAST RADIUS: cli_auth.go:200 feeds this into analytics.Identify as the PostHog PERSON PROPERTY cli_hours_active_7d (analytics.go:205). Wrong value propagates into every cohort, funnel and activation metric keyed on it.

FALSIFIABLE CHECK: the 7d window has 168 hours. Any user with cli_hours_active_7d > 168 proves the metric is broken. Run that query first.

FIX: COUNT(DISTINCT hour_bucket). One line + sqlc regen. Note isFirstRun/isReactivated in cliactivity.go are 0-vs-nonzero checks and are NOT affected.
notes:
ALREADY FIXED server-side on misc-coe branch ajit/misc-coe, commit 8b321224c:
  -SELECT COUNT(*) AS hours
  +SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hour_bucket) AS hours
plus the regenerated sqlc/auth.sql.go. Comment updated to 'Count distinct wall-clock hours, not per-repo rows within each hour.' Exactly the recommended fix. Not yet merged to main — verify it lands before trusting cli_hours_active_7d.
close_reason: Fixed server-side on ajit/misc-coe commit 8b321224c; tracking merge separately

title: cli_activity.repo_id means 'the URL named a repo', not 'the user worked in a repo'
description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified): cliactivity.go:77-81 sets repo_id ONLY from chi.URLParam(r,'repo_id'). TrackActivity is mounted on exactly one route group (router.go:2020, /api/v1/cli/*), and only ONE route in it has a {repo_id} param: GET /cli/repos/{repo_id}. Every other tracked route -- GET /cli/repos, GET /cli/doctor/context, POST /cli/friction, POST /cli/repo/init -- is structurally NULL.

So 68% NULL is not data loss, it is the schema working as designed. The column answers 'did the URL name a repo' while every consumer reads it as 'was the user active in this repo'.

DOWNSTREAM (verified): hq.sql GetCLIActivityScalars computes active_repos and active_teams as COUNT(DISTINCT repo_id) WHERE repo_id IS NOT NULL -- both undercount to only the repo-detail fetches.

FIX DIRECTION: ox knows config.GetRepoID(projectRoot) on every invocation but never puts it on the wire (useragent.SetHeaders sends only User-Agent, X-Orchestrator, traceparent). Send repo identity as a header; middleware prefers path param, falls back to header. Cross-repo + new wire contract -> needs Ryan review per CLAUDE.md 'API source of truth'.
notes:
CLI SIDE SHIPPED (ox repo, branch ajit/fix-telemetry-daemon). The header is INERT until api-go reads it.

WIRE CONTRACT — what ox now sends:
  Header: X-Sageox-Repo-Id
  Value:  the SageOx repo ID from .sageox/config.json (config.GetRepoID)
  Shape:  ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$  (validated CLI-side before emit)
  Sent on: every SageOx API request built through useragent.SetHeaders /
           useragent.NewRequest — internal/api, internal/auth,
           internal/doctorapi, internal/telemetry. Not git/LFS transport.
  Omitted (never empty) when: outside a project, repo not yet registered,
           value fails validation, or the process is the daemon.

DAEMON IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. It serves every workspace on the machine
from one process, so a process-global repo ID would stamp all its traffic
with whichever repo it started in — wrong data, not missing data. Daemon
rows stay repo-less. Regression test: internal/cli/repoid_test.go
TestNewContext_DaemonIsNotTaggedWithRepoID.

REMAINING api-go WORK (needs Ryan review — new wire contract):
  middleware/cliactivity/cliactivity.go, replace lines 77-81:
    if id := chi.URLParam(r, "repo_id"); id != "" {
        repoID = pgtype.Text{String: id, Valid: true}      // path wins
    } else if id := r.Header.Get("X-Sageox-Repo-Id"); id != "" {
        repoID = pgtype.Text{String: id, Valid: true}      // fall back
    }
  Re-validate server-side (do NOT trust the client's character class) and
  consider verifying the caller actually has access to that repo before
  storing it — the header is user-controlled input.

  Note the dedup key is (user_id, COALESCE(repo_id,''), hour_bucket), so
  once the header lands, hours that used to produce one NULL row will
  produce one repo row instead. That CHANGES the row shape feeding
  CountCLIActivityHours — fix ox-5bz3 (COUNT DISTINCT) at the same time or
  cli_hours_active_7d will shift for reasons unrelated to real usage.

title: ox daemon start --foreground poisons command latency telemetry

title: Fix OTLP exporter 401: attach JWT Bearer per-request
description: PR #1217 in sageox-monorepo (commit 4bc7356c3) JWT-gated /api/v1/otlp/* on 2026-05-14. CLI+daemon OTLP exporters in internal/observability/otel.go construct the otlptracehttp exporter with no auth header, so /api/v1/otlp/v1/traces returns 401 and trace batches are silently dropped (~174k 401s in last 30d Honeycomb). Fix: attach an auth RoundTripper via otlptracehttp.WithHTTPClient that pulls the current token from the local token store per-request (handles daemon long-running token rotation). Keep existing telemetry/endpoint gate; do not roll back server JWT-gating (intentional per audit ox-w9yc5).

Session recording for 2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO has three issues:

1. **Pre-session content included**: raw.jsonl starts at seq=0 with "switch to a new branch" — 3 entries BEFORE /ox-session-start was called (seq=3). The recording should only include content from AFTER ox agent session start completes.

2. **Session truncated at plan mode exit**: Recording ends at seq=32 "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" which corresponds to ExitPlanMode. The entire implementation phase is missing: parallel subagent execution (3 agents), code changes to 4 files, build/lint/test verification, beads issue management, git commit, git push, and PR creation. This is ~80% of the session value.

3. **Plan content not captured**: The plan was written to a file via the Write tool but the plan content itself doesn't appear in raw.jsonl (tool entries show [0 chars]). Similarly, all subagent results are absent.

## Expected Behavior

- raw.jsonl should NOT include any entries from before ox agent session start completes
- raw.jsonl should include ALL entries from session start up to (but not including) ox agent session stop  
- Tool results (especially Write, Task subagent results) should have their content captured, not [0 chars]

## Observed Behavior

- 33 entries in raw.jsonl, 3 of which predate session start
- Recording stops at ExitPlanMode (seq=32), missing the entire implementation
- Most tool results show [0 chars] content

Session: 2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO
Ledger path: ledger/sessions/2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO/
Local cache: Library/Caches/sageox/sessions/repo_019c5812.../sessions/2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO/

## Investigation Starting Points

- How does the session recorder hook into Claude Code's message stream?
- Is there a message buffer that gets flushed at session start (explaining pre-start content)?
- What causes the recording to stop mid-session? Is there a max entry count, a context compaction event, or does ExitPlanMode somehow signal an end?

title: Consolidate SessionMeta construction into shared builder
description:
There are 4 sites constructing lfs.SessionMeta inline with no shared code. This makes adding new fields (like user_id, repo_id) a 4-file change and risks drift between sites.

## Current Sites
1. cmd/ox/agent_session.go:829 — main session stop (richest: Model, Title, Summary)
2. cmd/ox/agent_session_recover.go:174 — recovery (subset: no Model, Title, Summary)
3. cmd/ox/session_upload_cmd.go:128 — manual upload (has its own buildSessionMeta helper)
4. cmd/ox/doctor_session_upload_retry.go:261 — doctor retry (copies from orphan.Meta)

## Proposed Approach
Add a builder/constructor to internal/lfs/meta.go that all sites use. Options:
- Functional options pattern: lfs.NewSessionMeta(name, opts...)
- Builder with required + optional fields
- Simple constructor with commonly-shared fields + setters for optional ones

The key insight: sites 1 and 2 both have agent state, site 4 copies from existing meta, site 3 reconstructs from dir name. A constructor with required fields (Version, SessionName, Username, AgentID, AgentType, CreatedAt, Files) plus chainable setters for optional fields (Model, Title, Summary, EntryCount) would cover all cases cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Single construction path for SessionMeta
- All 4 sites use the shared builder
- No behavioral change — existing meta.json output stays identical
- Adding a new field (like user_id) only requires changing the builder, not 4 files

title: fix: daemon persistLedgerPath writes empty path due to stale config cache
description:
## Symptom

`ox daemon status` shows ledger as 'synced' but `ox status` shows 'not cloned' for the same ledger path.

Observed on ~/Documents/Code/sageox/sageox-init where config.local.toml had:
```toml
[ledger]
path = ''
last_sync = 2026-02-18T06:10:41.576431Z
```

The daemon was syncing correctly (updating last_sync), but the path was empty — causing ox status to report 'not cloned'.

## Root Cause

Race condition between `persistLedgerPath()` and `UpdateConfigLastSync()` in the daemon. They use different config objects:

1. `persistLedgerPath()` loads a **fresh** config from disk via `config.LoadLocalConfig()`, writes `Path = '/correct/path'`, and saves to disk.
2. `UpdateConfigLastSync()` uses the workspace registry's in-memory `localConfigCache`, which still has `Ledger.Path == ''`.
3. When `UpdateConfigLastSync()` saves the stale cache to disk, it **overwrites** the path that `persistLedgerPath()` just wrote.

The sequence:
- Daemon starts, `localConfigCache` loaded with `Ledger == nil`
- `UpdateConfigLastSync('ledger')` creates `LedgerConfig{}` with empty Path in cache, saves to disk → `path = ''` in TOML
- `persistLedgerPath()` loads fresh config from disk, sees `Path == ''`, writes correct path to disk
- Next sync: `UpdateConfigLastSync('ledger')` saves cache (still has `Path == ''`) → overwrites the correct path

## Code Paths

**Daemon (works):** `WorkspaceRegistry.rebuildFromConfigLocked()` skips empty path, falls through to `InitializeLedger()` which computes the default path via `config.DefaultLedgerPath()`. Daemon knows the real path.

**ox status (broken):** `cmd/ox/status.go:1409` checks `localCfg.Ledger == nil` but NOT `localCfg.Ledger.Path == ''`. When the struct exists with empty path, the fallback to `ledger.DefaultPath()` never fires, and the `hasLedger` check at line 535 (`Path \!= ''`) is false → shows 'not cloned'.

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1: Root cause — persistLedgerPath should use the registry cache
Add `PersistLedgerPath(path)` method to `WorkspaceRegistry` that updates the `localConfigCache` directly, keeping it in sync with `UpdateConfigLastSync()`. Change `persistLedgerPath()` to call this instead of loading a separate config copy.

### Fix 2: Defensive — ox status should handle empty path
Change `cmd/ox/status.go:1409` from `localCfg.Ledger == nil` to `localCfg.Ledger == nil || localCfg.Ledger.Path == ''` so it falls back to default path discovery.

### Fix 3: Remove unused import
After fix 1, `internal/daemon/sync.go` no longer needs the `config` package import.

## Files Changed

- `internal/daemon/workspace_registry.go` — add `PersistLedgerPath()` method
- `internal/daemon/sync.go` — simplify `persistLedgerPath()`, remove unused config import
- `cmd/ox/status.go` — defensive empty-path fallback

title: Daemon polling is recorded as human CLI activity in cli_activity
description:
internal/api/repos.go builds every request with useragent.NewRequest -> useragent.String() = 'ox/<ver> (...)', the CLI User-Agent. The daemon calls GetRepos through that same client (internal/daemon/sync_discovery.go:67,140) for lazy credential refresh, so daemon-originated rows are indistinguishable from a human running ox.

Consequence: an unattended machine with a running daemon can register cli_activity hours with no human present, inflating CLI DAU and cli_hours_active_7d.

Separately, the paths that DO use useragent.DaemonString() ('ox-daemon/<ver> (...)') hit the version regex 'ox/(\\d+...)' in cliactivity.go:34, which does NOT match 'ox-daemon/' -- no literal 'ox/' substring. Those rows get cli_version=''. POST /api/v1/cli/friction from internal/daemon/friction.go:66 is tracked and lands exactly here. GetCLIVersionDistribution filters cli_version != '' so they silently vanish from the version histogram.

DECIDE: should daemon traffic count as CLI activity at all? If no, filter it out explicitly rather than relying on a regex miss. If yes, record a client_class column so daemon and human rows are separable.
notes:
CORRECTION to my earlier note: I assessed the WithDaemonUserAgent doc comment against sageox-monorepo/main and called its premise wrong. It is CORRECT against the branch it ships with. misc-coe (worktree, branch ajit/misc-coe) commit 8b321224c 'fix(analytics): count human CLI activity accurately' adds:

  func IsDaemonUserAgent(ua string) bool {
      return strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ua), "ox-daemon/")
  }

and short-circuits BOTH middlewares on it — cliactivity.TrackActivity (skips the cli_activity INSERT entirely) and middleware.CLIActivityTracker (skips the cli.api_call PostHog event). Its comment explicitly rejects relying on the ParseOxVersion regex miss: 'the parser's incidental behavior is not an activity policy.' That is the explicit exclusion I said was missing. My criticism applied to main only.

CLI-SIDE COVERAGE VERIFIED COMPLETE. Every endpoint under /api/v1/cli/* that the daemon can reach sends the daemon UA:
  /api/v1/cli/repos        GetRepos       sync_discovery.go:66,139   applyUserAgent repos.go:189
  /api/v1/cli/repos/{id}   GetRepoDetail  sync_discovery.go:240      applyUserAgent repos.go:332
  /api/v1/cli/settings     GetCLISettings sync_settings.go:59        applyUserAgent repos.go:411
  /api/v1/cli/friction     frictionax     daemon/friction.go:66      sets DaemonString directly
All four daemon RepoClient constructions call WithDaemonUserAgent(). No gap.

LATENT ISSUE (not a bug today): applyUserAgent is opt-in per method and only repos.go calls it. GetLedgerStatus (ledger.go) and the KB client do NOT, so a client explicitly marked as the daemon silently sends the interactive CLI UA from those methods. Harmless now because /api/v1/repos/{id}/ledger-status and /api/v1/kb are outside the /cli route group TrackActivity is mounted on. It becomes a silent leak the moment TrackActivity is mounted more broadly. Consider applying the UA centrally in one request-construction path instead of remembering it at each call site — same opt-in-you-must-remember shape as the rest of this thread.

title: Consolidate three diverged HTML generation paths into single pipeline
description:
Three separate HTML rendering pipelines have diverged, causing repeated bugs where fixes to one path don't apply to others (see ox-aql).

**Current state — three paths:**

| Path | File | Used by | Template |
|------|------|---------|----------|
| 1 | internal/session/html/ | ox session stop, ox agent <id> session stop | Embedded assets |
| 2 | cmd/ox/session_html.go | ox session export, ox session push-summary | Inline const strings |
| 3 | cmd/ox/session_view_html.go | ox session view --html | Inline const strings |

**Duplicated logic (copy-pasted, then diverged):**
- Entry type mapping (mapEntryType vs viewHTMLMapEntryType vs normalizeMessageType)
- Role-to-type mapping
- HTML escaping, output truncation
- Title generation
- Timestamp parsing (ts vs timestamp, RFC3339 vs RFC3339Nano)
- Root-level vs nested content extraction
- CSS/JS (inline strings in paths 2+3, embedded assets in path 1)

**Missing from some paths:**
- Path 1: no diff rendering, no collapsible tool messages
- Path 3: no sender labels, no summary/aha moments, no keyboard shortcuts
- Path 2: uses local openInBrowser() instead of cli.OpenInBrowser (canonical violation)
- Path 3: dead code (processContentWithMermaid — defined, never called)

**Proposed approach:**
Converge on a single rendering pipeline in internal/session/html/ that all command paths feed into, with options struct for toggling features (summary panel, sender labels, aha moments, etc.). Entry type mapping, timestamp parsing, content extraction, and CSS/JS live in one place.
notes:
## Test Coverage Audit

**Path 3 (session_view_html.go) has ZERO tests** — this is the path where all three rendering bugs in ox-aql were found. No tests for viewHTMLBuildMessageView, viewHTMLMapEntryType, viewHTMLMapRoleToType, or any of the viewHTML* functions.

**Markdown generator (internal/session/markdown.go) has ZERO tests** — the MarkdownGenerator used by session stop/export has no JSONL-in → markdown-out tests at all.

### What needs testing (minimum):

1. **viewHTMLMapEntryType** — table-driven test covering user, assistant, message, tool_call, tool_result, tool, system, unknown (this is where the bug was)
2. **viewHTMLBuildMessageView** — test with:
   - Root-level content (imported JSONL format)
   - Nested data.content (standard format)
   - ts field (imported) vs timestamp field (standard)
   - user/assistant/tool entry types at root level
3. **viewHTMLBuildTemplateData** — end-to-end: _meta header + entries → template data with correct metadata, message count, types
4. **MarkdownGenerator.Generate** — JSONL session → markdown output, verify entries appear with correct formatting
5. **Cross-format integration tests** — same JSONL input through all three HTML paths should produce equivalent content (different styling is fine, missing entries is not)

### Consolidation reduces test burden:
Once paths converge into single pipeline (the main fix), these duplicated test concerns collapse into one test suite.
close_reason: Tracked by epic ox-iz9 which has detailed subtasks. This was the initial analysis issue that spawned the epic.

2. [OPEN] viewHTMLMapEntryType doesn't recognize 'user' or 'assistant' entry types — imported JSONL uses type='user' and type='assistant' at root level. title: ox plan review inflates the command-latency tail (human think-time)

Their reported duration is therefore human think-time, not ox latency — legitimate wall-clock, but it fattens the p99 tail of command latency.

Decide whether to (a) leave as-is, (b) annotate them cli.AnnotationLongRunning: 'true' so they drop out of command-duration telemetry, or (c) keep the event but split interactive commands into their own aggregate. Check the real distribution in Honeycomb before deciding — unlike the daemon, this may be low-volume enough not to matter.
